definitions.meaning: a poetic or dialect word for a small lake or pond
as an adjective the word means only, no more than

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a body of water as just a lake and nothing more.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard dictionary meanings: a still pool of water, and the adjective for something slight or bare.

clue.text: Pays for outside of tyre to get soft tread

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it, so pays for gives foots

indicators.note: the outside of a word is its first and last letters only, taken from tyre here

parts.note: p (piano) is the musical abbreviation for soft

explanation.surface: A motorist pays for new tyres to get a softer tread on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside of' takes the first and last letters of 'tyre', giving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A single tread is one step of the foot, so the noun tread works as a synonym.

clue.text: Papa is the French for this kitchen utensil

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
in French the word is is est
in French the word the (masculine) is le

explanation.surface: A cookery quiz asks for the French word for a kitchen tool, with Papa as a clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A pounding tool used with a mortar to crush spices is a standard kitchen utensil.

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant is to take short gasping breaths

explanation.surface: An out-of-control man pauses to catch his breath, panting.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unchecked and spreading wildly, like rampant inflation, is unrestrained.

clue.text: Bachelor of Engineering can be cultivated and not entirely unacceptable

parts.note: BE is the abbreviation for the degree Bachelor of Engineering
arable land is land that can be ploughed and farmed

explanation.surface: An engineering graduate's farmland is grudgingly judged passable.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tolerable is just about acceptable, so not entirely unacceptable is a playful paraphrase.

indicators.note: lacking says a letter is missing from the word for destitute people

parts.note: paupers are very poor, destitute people
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: Homeless people lack the identification documents officials demand.
explanation.walkthrough: U for 'acceptable' is the old upper-class label (U and non-U).
explanation.definitionFit: Identity documents are commonly called one's papers, as in 'show me your papers'.

clue.text: Obstructs openings of basement air raid shelters

indicators.note: openings means the first letter of each of the following four words

explanation.surface: Something is blocking the entrances to underground air raid shelters.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar a way is to block it, so the verb is a synonym for obstructs.

indicators.note: cook means fiddle or falsify, so the remaining letters are rearranged
to skin something removes its outer layer, here the first and last letters of frozen

explanation.surface: A recipe instruction: take a frozen duck, skin it and cook it.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinning 'frozen' leaves ROZE, which 'cook' rearranges. 'duck' looks like the bird but is the cricket score of nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a duck is a batsman's score of nil, from the egg shape of a nought.

clue.text: Remove signs of age with special drug

parts.note: an era is an age or period of history
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An advert promises to remove the signs of ageing with a special treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: To wipe something out leaves no trace of it, so to rub out is to remove signs of it.

indicators.note: a comeback means the word for king comes back, read in reverse

parts.note: a raja is an Indian king or prince

explanation.surface: A king makes his comeback at a golf tournament, the Open.
explanation.definitionFit: A door that is slightly open is described with this adjective.

definitions.meaning: an imperative slang phrase meaning go away
read as three words, ... is a euphemism for having sex

explanation.surface: Someone is told to leave so others can make love.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the letters as BE AT IT.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for clear off, and split differently a coy euphemism for being engaged in sex.

indicators.note: rejected means the word for agent is turned back on itself

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is a sales agent
poets write verse

explanation.surface: A contrary literary agent turns down a poet's manuscript.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone perverse deliberately acts against what is reasonable, which is to be contrary.

parts.note: to pan a show is to criticise it harshly
the is the definite article
on means about, as in a book on birds

explanation.surface: A critic slates a newspaper article about a temple.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pantheon in Rome is a temple to all the gods, and the word names such temples generally.

clue.text: A cereal said to blow your mind

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken and the matching sound is spelt differently

parts.note: maize is a cereal crop, so a cereal is a maize

explanation.surface: A breakfast cereal is advertised as mind-blowing.
explanation.definitionFit: To astonish someone completely is to blow their mind, a colloquial synonym.

indicators.note: dividing means the word for question splits the word for speculation apart

parts.note: a bet is a speculation or gamble
to ask is to question

explanation.surface: A disputed goal splits opinion among those speculating on the match.
explanation.definitionFit: In basketball the goal is the hoop and net, which is called by this name.

clue.text: Pull out and overtake wildly, missing road traffic accident

indicators.note: wildly says the letters of overtake are scrambled, once some are taken away

parts.note: RTA is the standard abbreviation for road traffic accident

explanation.surface: A driver pulls out and overtakes recklessly, narrowly avoiding a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes R, T and A from OVERTAKE, leaving OVEKE for 'wildly' to rearrange. 'Pull out' looks like driving but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke a memory or feeling is to draw or call it out, hence pull out.

clue.text: Service provider to show surprise about good performance at last

parts.note: to gasp is to show surprise

indicators.note: about means the word for good is turned round

parts.note: pi, short for pious, means good

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of performance

explanation.surface: A utility company gasps in surprise at finally performing well.
explanation.definitionFit: A pipe that carries the gas supply into a building literally provides the service.

indicators.note: surrounding means the word for vexation goes round the other letters

parts.note: pique is irritation or vexation

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of shy are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a shy person's odd appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vexation' and 'figure' both read as feelings or numbers at first; 'strangely' rearranges the shy letters before 'surrounding' wraps them.
explanation.definitionFit: One's bodily build or shape is one's figure, a synonym.

parts.note: in Genesis Eve is the first woman
to lop is to cut off

explanation.surface: A president's wife makes a cut to an advance on some day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' suggests a president's wife, but here it is the first woman, Eve.
explanation.definitionFit: To advance and to grow or progress are near-synonyms, as in a plan that develops.

clue.text: Dig up old wine by hollow tree

parts.note: ex means former or old
cava is a Spanish sparkling wine

indicators.note: hollow means the inside of tree is emptied, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone unearths an old bottle of wine buried beside a hollow tree.
explanation.definitionFit: To excavate is to remove earth to uncover things, as archaeologists dig up remains.

clue.text: Headless corpse on ship starts to enter yearlong journey

indicators.note: headless removes the first letter from the word for corpse

parts.note: a body is a corpse
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

indicators.note: starts to picks the first letters of the next two words

explanation.surface: A grisly tale of a headless corpse aboard ship on a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Headless' drops the first letter of BODY; 'starts to' takes the initials of 'enter' and 'yearlong'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homer's Odyssey tells of Odysseus's ten-year voyage home, so the word means a long adventurous trip.

clue.text: Jellied eel covered in blubber and veg

indicators.note: covered in means the scrambled eel goes inside the word for blubber

parts.note: to blubber is to cry noisily

indicators.note: jellied means the letters of eel are set into a new shape

explanation.surface: A menu of jellied eels in fat served with vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jellied' reads as cooking but rearranges the fish's letters; jellied eels are a traditional London East End dish.
explanation.definitionFit: This crisp green stalk is a common vegetable, and veg is short for vegetable.

indicators.note: section signals that the answer is a part cut from the words master ran disciplined

explanation.surface: A taskmaster ran a strictly controlled department.
explanation.definitionFit: A short job or trip to do something for someone is a task of this kind.

parts.note: ejected means thrown up, so vomited

explanation.surface: A miserable daughter has been sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling low and downcast is a synonym for being sad at heart.

parts.note: a jerk is an irritating or stupid man

explanation.surface: An irritating man wearing an overly snug waistcoat.
explanation.definitionFit: A close-fitting sleeveless jacket, often of leather, worn especially in past centuries.

clue.text: Girl next door narrowly avoided collision

parts.note: something next door is near
a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.surface: A girl from the next house only just escaped a crash.
explanation.definitionFit: A noun for an incident in which a crash was only just avoided, a standard phrase.

indicators.note: oddly deficient means the odd-numbered letters of repairing are dropped, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: Mending a pocket that was full of holes.
explanation.definitionFit: To pocket money is to take or gain it, a synonym for being paid for work.

clue.text: Tango with admirer, turn and rise up

indicators.note: turn means the combined letters are turned round and read backwards

parts.note: Tango is T in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a lover is an admirer

explanation.surface: Dancing the tango with an admirer, a couple twirl and lift.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebel against authority is to rise up, the verb sense of the word.

clue.text: Swelling fruit's first to fall down

indicators.note: first to fall down means the opening letter drops to the bottom of this down entry

parts.note: a plum is a fruit

explanation.surface: A bruise appears from fruit dropping from a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump or protuberance on the body is a swelling.

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for lease is cut off

parts.note: to rent is to lease

explanation.surface: A sailor signs a short-term lease ashore.
explanation.walkthrough: A Wren was a member of the Women's Royal Naval Service, Britain's former navy branch for women.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the former British women's naval service was known by this name, so a sailor.

indicators.note: somehow says the letters of true are arranged in some other way

parts.note: I is an abbreviation for independence or independent

explanation.surface: Body organs that in some way show real independence.
explanation.definitionFit: The womb is an organ, and this is the Latin plural for wombs.

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Where a black cat is laid to rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A grave or vault is a final resting place for the dead.
